### Pie chart
Parts of a whole drawn as slices from a data table, as a pie or a donut with its total.

Component ID: `pie-chart`

[Component documentation](https://www.expressivecss.com/pie-chart.html.md) · [Repository source](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/blob/master/docs/src/pages/pie-chart.astro) · [Matching tag](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/tree/v0.20.0)

Contract: ExpressiveCSS 0.20.0

Contract SHA-256: `9572eb9544e6bc2b462220e2535968147b0c19ca83f15ac6481f8e5cb70d07f4`

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Public JavaScript exports: `PieChart`. See the [API index](../references/api-index.md).

Example: Revenue split across three plans, with the total in the middle, is a donut pie chart. Revenue from twelve sources is a bar chart.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Support: Slices drawn clockwise from the top from a figure's data table, with a legend of each row's cell and share, donut, values and sparkline modifiers, a <tfoot> total in the donut hole, labels with each slice's name outside it, further columns in the tooltip, and a pointer and keyboard tooltip that highlights the slice.

Web adaptation: The <table> stays in the page as the text alternative and the no-JavaScript fallback; the slices, values, total and legend are aria-hidden and the plot is one Tab stop with a polite live tooltip.

Known boundary: Zero and negative values have no slice. The .labels names only move up or down their side, so many thin slices near the top or bottom can run into the caption or legend unless data-other groups them.

Full parity remains unassessed. Review provenance and specification links: [capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#pie-chart).

#### Contract

A `<figure class="pie-chart">` takes the same `<figcaption>` and `<table>` as a column chart. `AutoInit()` draws the first value column as slices of the total, clockwise from the top in table order, with a legend of every row, its cell and its share, and a tooltip that follows the pointer round the pie. The table stays in the page, visually hidden, as the chart's text alternative; without JavaScript it shows instead of the chart.

#### Syntax

```html
<figure class="pie-chart donut">
  <figcaption>Lead sources, last six months</figcaption>
  <table>
    <thead>
      <tr><th>Source</th><th>Leads</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><th>Referrals</th><td>558</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Organic search</th><td>434</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Paid campaigns</th><td>248</td></tr>
    </tbody>
    <tfoot>
      <tr><th>Total leads</th><td>1,240</td></tr>
    </tfoot>
  </table>
</figure>
```

#### Also documented

The Pie chart section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Tokens.

#### Rules

- `pie-chart-is-a-figure-with-a-table`: Write .pie-chart as a <figure> holding a <table> of the data. The drawn chart is hidden from assistive technology, so the table is all a screen reader reads, and it is what shows without JavaScript.
- `pie-chart-has-a-caption`: Name a .pie-chart with a <figcaption>. It names the focusable plot as well as the figure; hide it with .visually-hidden when nearby text already names the chart.
